title: The causative
subtitle: have something done — arranging for someone else to do it

blocks.text: Form: subject + **have** in the correct form + object + past participle. We use this to show that someone arranges for someone else to do something for them.

rows.example: Mrs Taylor **has her car cleaned** once a month.
She **is having the tyres checked** at the moment.
This is not usually used in the causative.
She **had the car filled up** with petrol yesterday.
She **was having the car repaired** when I last saw her.
This is not usually used in the causative.
She **will have a car alarm fitted** when she can afford it. She **would have air bags put in** but it's too expensive.
She **is going to have a new car radio installed**.
She might stop **having the car cleaned** so often.

blocks.intro: Look at the difference between a normal active sentence and a sentence in the causative.
items: Normal active sentence: Someone **cleans** Mrs Taylor's car every week.
In the causative: Mrs Taylor **has her car cleaned** every week.

blocks.intro: We can also use **get** instead of **have**. **Get** is more informal than **have**.
items: I'm going to **have** my hair cut tomorrow. (more formal)
I'm going to **get** my hair cut tomorrow. (more informal)
Just as with the passive (see Unit 11), we can use **by** to show who does the action.
We're having a family photo taken **by** a local photographer.

blocks.text: With the causative, **have** always comes **before** the noun and the past participle always comes **after** the noun.

blocks.correct: Did you **have the furniture delivered** yesterday?
blocks.incorrect: Did you **have delivered the furniture** yesterday?

items: Some verbs have irregular past participle forms.

exercises.title: A · Rewrite with have
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the correct form of have so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence.

items.prompt:
Let's arrange for someone to knock that wall down.
Let's ___ that wall knocked down.
acceptedAnswers: have
Let's have that wall knocked down.
Let's have that wall knocked down

items.prompt:
We paid someone to deliver the furniture.
We ___ the furniture delivered.
acceptedAnswers: had
We had the furniture delivered.
We had the furniture delivered

items.prompt:
I'm going to pay someone to paint this wall.
I'm ___ this wall painted.
acceptedAnswers: going to have
I'm going to have this wall painted.
I'm going to have this wall painted

items.prompt:
Has anyone printed the invitations for you yet?
___ you ___ the invitations printed yet?
acceptedAnswers: Have / had
Have you had the invitations printed yet?
Have you had the invitations printed yet

items.prompt:
You should arrange for someone to fix your mobile.
You should ___ your mobile fixed.
acceptedAnswers: have
You should have your mobile fixed.
You should have your mobile fixed

items.prompt:
When did you dye your hair?
When ___ you ___ your hair dyed?
acceptedAnswers: did / have
When did you have your hair dyed?
When did you have your hair dyed

items.prompt:
A vet is looking at Lucy at the moment.
They ___ Lucy looked at by a vet at the moment.
acceptedAnswers: are having
're having
They are having Lucy looked at by a vet at the moment.

items.prompt:
I haven't taken my suit to the dry-cleaner's yet.
I ___ my suit dry-cleaned yet.
acceptedAnswers: haven't had
have not had
I haven't had my suit dry-cleaned yet.
I haven't had my suit dry-cleaned yet
